summary: 4-channel professional club mixer with built-in USB sound card (multi-channel), rekordbox and Serato DVS support, and USB MIDI control.
identityNotes: No ambiguity on the model. Official MIDI list and manual were not retrievable (hosts blocked); a mirrored manual PDF exists but could not be fetched. MIDI map is therefore learn-mode.

tests.title: DJM-A9 Windows driver installed and healthy
tests.why: Without the Pioneer DJ ASIO driver the device falls back to generic Windows audio (high latency, missing channels) or does not appear in DJ software.
steps: Connect the device by USB and power it on.
Run the check; it matches Device Manager names against the profile.
If not present, install the current driver from Pioneer DJ support and reboot.

pass.source: DeckChek test definition (not a manufacturer spec)

tests.title: Driver signed, status OK and ASIO registered
tests.why: Unsigned or errored drivers cause crackles, disconnects and ASIO devices missing from the DJ software audio menu.
steps: Run the driver check after the device is powered.
Review signed / status / ASIO registration results.

pass.source: DeckChek test definition (not a manufacturer spec)

tests.title: DJM-A9 firmware version up to date
tests.why: Old firmware can cause MIDI/jog/DVS faults fixed in later releases.
steps: Open the Pioneer DJ firmware/updater utility for DJM-A9, or the DJ software settings page that shows firmware.
Note installed firmware version and compare with latest on the Pioneer DJ support page (not auto-checked; version unverified in research).
Tick when firmware is current or update completed.

tests.title: rekordbox installed, no recent crashes
tests.why: Crashes or log errors in rekordbox often explain dropouts that look like hardware faults.
steps: Run the rekordbox log scan.
Review crash count (90 days) and log errors.

pass.source: DeckChek test definition (not a manufacturer spec)

tests.title: Serato DJ Pro installed, no recent crashes
tests.why: Crashes or log errors in Serato DJ Pro often explain dropouts that look like hardware faults.
steps: Run the Serato DJ Pro log scan.
Review crash count (90 days) and log errors.

pass.source: DeckChek test definition (not a manufacturer spec)

tests.title: Master output signal health
tests.why: Checks XLR/RCA master path.
steps: Play a test tone from USB ch1 in your DJ software.
Connect MASTER to an audio interface.
Run Signal health for 10 s.

tests.title: Booth output signal health
tests.why: Booth out feeds the DJ monitor.
steps: Connect BOOTH out to an interface.
Run with tone on master.

tests.title: Headphone output L/R
tests.why: Dead channel on headphones.
steps: Cue a channel, listen on both sides, or measure with adapter.

tests.title: Ground and hum (master)
tests.why: Ground loops and poor grounds.
steps: All channels down, master up.
Run Ground & hum; connect and disconnect turntable ground wires.

tests.title: USB ASIO round-trip latency
tests.why: Checks driver buffer behaviour.
steps: Route USB ch1 output to a mixer line input via a loop of the master out into a LINE input.
Run measurement at buffer 128/256.

tests.title: Channel 1 USB return signal health
tests.why: Verifies channel 1 returns audio to the DJ software on the USB sound card.
steps: Set CH1 input selector to USB.
Play a stereo test tone to CH1.
Run Signal health on the channel's USB return/master.

tests.title: Channel 1 analog input (phono/line) signal health
tests.why: Checks the A/D path used for DVS.
steps: Connect a deck or player to CH1 analog input; set selector to PHONO or LINE accordingly.
Play a source.
Run Signal health on its USB return.

tests.title: Timecode check CH1 (Serato CV02.5)
tests.why: Verifies DVS on this channel: carrier, phase, balance.
steps: Connect a turntable with Serato control vinyl to CH1 PHONO input and enable DVS channel mapping.
Play vinyl at 33 rpm, pitch 0.

tests.title: Timecode check CH2 (Serato CV02.5)
tests.why: Verifies DVS on this channel: carrier, phase, balance.
steps: Connect a turntable with Serato control vinyl to CH2 PHONO input and enable DVS channel mapping.
Play vinyl at 33 rpm, pitch 0.

tests.title: DVS signal integrity (generic)
tests.why: Checks dropouts/imbalance on DVS channel.
steps: Play control vinyl; scratch 20 s.
Run DVS signal.

tests.title: Channel L/R balance and hum per channel
tests.why: Stereo imbalance or hum on individual channels.
steps: Feed identical stereo tone to each channel.
Set trims/faders/EQ flat.
Run Signal health per channel and compare.

tests.title: Isolator / EQ band cut check
tests.why: Dead or leaking EQ bands.
steps: Play pink noise or a sweep through a channel.
Cut LOW, MID, HI in turn and confirm each band drops.
Repeat on all channels.

tests.title: MIDI coverage: every control reports
tests.why: A dead control (broken pot, fader track, switch, pad) never sends MIDI.
steps: Open the MIDI test and select this device's MIDI port.
Exercise every control once in sequence, each pad/button/knob/fader.
Review any control not seen and any unexpected message.

pass.source: DeckChek test definition (not a manufacturer spec)

tests.title: Switch bounce / stuck check (cue, FX and assign buttons)
tests.why: Worn switches double-trigger (bounce) or stick, causing false cue/play triggers.
steps: Press each button/pad once firmly, then once lightly.
Hold one for 3 seconds then release.
Review bounce count and stuck state.

pass.source: DeckChek test definition (not a manufacturer spec)

tests.title: Channel, FX and meter LEDs light correctly
tests.why: Dead LEDs hide state (cue, loop, pad bank).
steps: Start the LED test; the app lights each LED.
Confirm each lights and has the expected colour/brightness; mark failures.

tests.title: Crossfader: full travel, monotonic, low jitter
tests.why: Worn tracks or dirty pots cause jumps, dead zones or jitter. Magnetic/contactless wear still shows as jitter or cut-out.
steps: Move Crossfader slowly end to end, then back, three times.
Pause at the middle for 2 seconds.
Review min/max, monotonicity, jitter and resolution.

tests.title: MIDI timing jitter under constant motion
tests.why: Timing jitter or USB hub congestion makes jogs/scratching feel uneven.
steps: Connect the device directly to a PC USB port (no hub).
Rotate the main continuous control at a steady speed for 10 seconds.
Review inter-message jitter.

tests.title: EQ and Color FX knobs sweep (all channels)
tests.why: Noisy pots.
steps: Sweep HI, MID, LOW and COLOR FX on each channel (repeat per control id).
Review jitter.

tests.title: Crossfader and channel fader feel
tests.why: Dirty/worn faders.
steps: Crossfader cuts cleanly at both ends and moves smoothly.
Channel faders no side-play.
Curve selectors work.

tests.title: Rear connectors and USB
tests.why: Dropouts from loose jacks.
steps: XLR/RCA/TRS jacks firm.
USB B and USB C seated.
Phono/line selectors and ground screws OK.
Mic inputs and level knobs work.

tests.title: Knobs, jog dial, buttons
tests.why: Wear.
steps: Knobs not loose or wobbly.
Encoder/jog dial clicks correctly.
No sticky buttons.
